title: Behavioral Health Scenario 11 – Emergency Department Suicide Identification, Assessment, Safety, and Follow-Up
narrative:
Scenario 11.1 – Patient Narrative
Maria, a 28-year-old with chronic pain and recent job loss, presents to a general medical emergency department (ED) for severe insomnia and anxiety. During triage, the nurse administers an ED-appropriate suicide risk screener (e.g., C-SSRS ED Screener with Triage Points or ASQ). Maria endorses suicidal ideation and reports a recent self-harm behavior.

The EHR captures screener responses as discrete structured data, derives an outcome (negative / non-acute positive / acute positive) using configurable rules, and then:
• Communicates status to the whole ED team via a visible ED trackboard / chart banner indicator, and
• Separately routes time-sensitive protocol work via role-based Tasks and a clinician-facing advisory that provides one-click access to the appropriate order set/checklists.

For positive screens, the EHR supports rapid mitigation (environment/room clearance checklist, belongings documentation, and observation/1:1 sitter workflow with appropriate provider authorization), followed by brief assessment and/or full suicide risk assessment (e.g., Brief Suicide Safety Assessment when ASQ is used; SAFE-T with C-SSRS when indicated).

Following assessment, the care team determines Maria can be discharged with collaborative safety planning, lethal means counseling, and rapid follow-up. At discharge, the EHR automatically includes (and prints or portal-delivers) a patient-facing safety plan and suicide-specific discharge instructions with crisis resources, and transmits a transition-of-care packet to outpatient providers while initiating post-discharge caring contacts/follow-up calls.

sections.heading: Scenario 11.2 – Screening and Identification
sections.narrative: In the ED, suicide risk screening is performed early (often at triage) using a validated tool appropriate to age and setting. The EHR supports fast capture of structured screening results, applies rules to identify positive/acute screens, and (a) communicates screening status via visible indicators and (b) routes the next required steps as time-sensitive tasks/advisories without relying on clinician memory.

steps.event: Administer suicide risk screener at triage (staff-administered or patient self-report)
steps.inputs: Validated suicide screening instrument (e.g., C-SSRS ED Screener or ASQ); respondent identity; encounter context
steps.outputs: QuestionnaireResponse with discrete item responses; completion timestamp; screener type/version; respondent identity
steps.actions: Nurse administers the ED-appropriate suicide screener; responses are captured as discrete values and submitted to the EHR
steps.profileBinding: SPiER ASQ Questionnaire ([built](../../FHIR-Resources/ASQ/)) or C-SSRS Screener ([built](../../FHIR-Resources/C-SSRS/))

steps.event: Retain suicide screening result as structured data
steps.inputs: Suicide screening QuestionnaireResponse (item-level responses)
steps.outputs: Persisted QuestionnaireResponse linked to ED Encounter; provenance/audit metadata
steps.actions: EHR validates and persists the structured QuestionnaireResponse; links it to the encounter and applies access controls
steps.walkthroughGapReason: Persistence has no separate narration in the demo: the QuestionnaireResponse referenced by 11.2-1A is the persisted resource.

steps.event: Auto-classify screening outcome (negative / non-acute positive / acute positive) and derive configurable risk tier
steps.inputs: Screening item responses; local stratification rules by setting/age; clinician override (if allowed)
steps.outputs: Discrete screening outcome + risk tier with timestamp; reason/override metadata (if clinician overrides)
steps.actions: EHR applies configurable rules to derive an outcome/risk tier from screener responses and records the result as discrete data
ehrsFm: DC.2.4.1 Support for Standard Care Plans
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — needs a SPiER ASQ Outcome Observation profile (low/non-acute positive/acute positive)

steps.event: Communicate suicide screening status to the ED team (trackboard + chart banner)
steps.inputs: Screening outcome/risk tier; patient context; local display rules
steps.outputs: Visible ED trackboard icon and/or chart banner indicator reflecting screening status; audit trail of status changes
steps.actions: EHR displays a prominent indicator (separate from workflow tasking) so all ED roles can recognize current screening status at a glance

reviewNotes.author: Kelly Samuelson
reviewNotes.text: storyboard - need the vendor agnostic version of this and then EHR specialist can translate this per EHR

steps.event: Route protocol work via Tasks/advisories and provide one-click access to relevant order set/checklists
steps.inputs: Screening outcome/risk tier; local ED protocol rules; staffing/role assignments; patient location
steps.outputs: Role-routed Tasks/notifications (e.g., notify ED provider, initiate safety mitigation checklist, request BH consult, schedule BSSA when applicable); acceptance/override reason capture
steps.actions: EHR creates role-based Tasks and, where configured, launches a staff advisory that links directly to the appropriate protocol order set/checklists
ehrsFm: DC.2.4.3 Support for Standard Care Plans, Guidelines, Protocols
steps.profileBinding: SPiER PlanDefinition for stage-1 → stage-2 transition ([`pathway-stages.fsh`](../../ig/input/fsh/pathway-stages.fsh))

sections.summary: **Screening and identification** — triage-time ASQ or C-SSRS ED screener, captured as discrete data, classified, surfaced on the trackboard, and routed via role-based tasks.
sections.note: **Open profile work:** ASQ Outcome Observation, Suicide-Screening-Status Flag. Both feed back to issue [#52](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/52) as non-Questionnaire workflow artifacts.

sections.heading: Scenario 11.3 – Immediate Safety / Mitigation
sections.narrative: For acute positive or otherwise high-risk presentations, the ED must rapidly mitigate environmental and procedural risks. The EHR supports a standardized mitigation checklist/order set, documents observation level and environmental safety actions, and ensures provider authorization/countersignature where required.

steps.event: Initiate immediate safety mitigation (keep patient in sight; move to room; start mitigation checklist)
steps.inputs: Positive screen/risk tier; local ED suicide safety protocol; current bed/room assignment
steps.outputs: Started mitigation checklist/Tasks; documentation that patient moved to a safer setting and not left unattended (when indicated)
steps.actions: Nurse initiates immediate mitigation per protocol and opens the mitigation checklist in the EHR to track required actions and handoffs
ehrsFm: DC.2.4.3 Support for Standard Care Plans

steps.event: Authorize and tailor suicide precaution / observation orders (with required signature/countersignature)
steps.inputs: Risk tier; nursing mitigation status; local order set defaults; patient-specific medical needs (lines, monitoring, imaging, etc.)
steps.outputs: Signed orders for precautions (including observation level and parameters); ordered consults; order modifications with rationale
steps.actions: Provider reviews recommended protocol orders, tailors parameters to the patient, and signs/countersigns as required (EHR enforces role-based ordering and captures rationale for deviations)
steps.fhirText: `ServiceRequest` (suicide precautions, observation level) with required signature

steps.event: Complete and document environmental safety / room clearance checklist and belongings security
steps.inputs: Room clearance checklist content; patient belongings inventory; local ligature/sharps risk guidance
steps.outputs: Completed checklist (time, performer, verifier); belongings secured record; exceptions documented with mitigation plan
steps.actions: Team completes room clearance and belongings safety steps (remove/secure potentially harmful items, cords/tubing not needed for care, sharps containers, etc.) and documents completion in a structured checklist
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — Room Clearance Checklist profile; Belongings Inventory profile

steps.event: Begin continuous observation when indicated; document observations and safety checks
steps.inputs: Observation order/level; patient location; observer role assignment; documentation frequency rules
steps.outputs: Observation documentation record (time-stamped entries); observer identity/competency; handoff log
steps.actions: A qualified observer provides continuous visual observation per policy when the patient is high-risk in an environment with safety hazards; the observer documents at the required interval and escalates concerns immediately

steps.event: Persist and display active safety precautions (incl. observation level, checklist completion, and observer assignment)
steps.inputs: Orders/Tasks for mitigation; completed checklist; observation order/level; observer assignment
steps.outputs: Active precaution status indicator (e.g., "Suicide precautions ON" + observation level) + checklist/observer status on trackboard/banner; audit trail
steps.actions: EHR stores active precautions and their current parameters, displays them on ED views, and maintains an audit trail of when precautions were started/changed/ended
steps.walkthroughGapReason: The demo emits no Flag resource, so there is no active-precautions indicator to narrate.

sections.summary: **Immediate safety / mitigation** — environmental safety, observation/sitter, belongings security.
sections.note: **Open profile work:** Mitigation Checklist, Suicide Precaution Order, Room Clearance Checklist, Belongings Inventory, Continuous Observation Log, Active Precautions Flag. All flow to issue [#52](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/52).

sections.heading: Scenario 11.4 – Brief Assessment and Suicide Risk Assessment
sections.narrative: After a positive screen, a trained clinician completes a brief suicide safety assessment (especially when ASQ is used and the screen is non-acute positive) to determine next steps. When indicated, the care team completes a structured suicide risk assessment (e.g., SAFE-T with C-SSRS). The EHR captures key assessment elements as discrete data and supports disposition decision-making.

steps.event: Complete Brief Suicide Safety Assessment (BSSA) after positive screen (as applicable)
steps.inputs: Screening results (incl. acuity); relevant history; current presentation; collateral info when available
steps.outputs: Structured BSSA record (discrete elements + narrative) including frequency of suicidal thoughts, plan/intent, past behavior, symptoms, supports/stressors, and means access; recommended next step
steps.actions: Clinician completes a brief assessment to triage next steps (e.g., urgent full mental health evaluation vs proceed with ED discharge planning with interventions) and documents key elements as structured data
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — needs FSH for BSSA ([TL-005](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/21), status:planned, promote priority)

steps.event: Record BSSA outcome and route next steps (full evaluation vs proceed to discharge pathway)
steps.inputs: BSSA findings; clinician determination; local clinical pathway rules
steps.outputs: Disposition routing Tasks (e.g., STAT mental health evaluation, BH consult); updated risk status indicator; documentation of "cannot leave until evaluated" status when applicable
steps.actions: EHR persists the BSSA, updates ED-visible indicators, and triggers the next protocol stage based on the clinician's determination and local pathway rules
steps.walkthroughGapReason: The demo records the BSSA (11.4-0A) but emits no routing Task, so there is no artifact for this step.
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — BSSA Outcome Observation; "Hold for Evaluation" Flag

steps.event: Complete structured suicide risk assessment (e.g., SAFE-T with C-SSRS) when indicated
steps.inputs: Screening + BSSA results (if performed); relevant prior history (prior attempts, diagnoses, substance use, meds); current presentation
steps.outputs: Structured risk assessment record (discrete elements + clinician narrative) including ideation severity, intent/plan, recent behavior, protective factors, and means access
steps.actions: Clinician completes a structured assessment in the EHR and documents key elements as discrete data to support risk determination and disposition planning

steps.event: Record suicide risk level/status and update ED-visible and longitudinal indicators
steps.inputs: Structured assessment data; clinician determination
steps.outputs: Discrete current suicide risk level/status (e.g., low/moderate/high/imminent) with timestamp; persistent risk indicator; optional coded diagnosis/problem entry
steps.actions: EHR persists the risk level as a longitudinal data element, updates ED banner/trackboard indicators, and triggers downstream workflows per policy
steps.fhirText: `Observation` (current suicide risk level) + `Condition` (suicide-risk condition, coded) + `Flag` (longitudinal risk indicator)
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — Current Suicide Risk Level Observation; Longitudinal Risk Flag

sections.summary: **Brief assessment and risk assessment** — BSSA (after positive ASQ) and SAFE-T with C-SSRS when indicated.
sections.note: **Gating tools:** BSSA (#21) and SAFE-T (#22) must move from `status:planned` to `status:built` to satisfy this section.

sections.heading: Scenario 11.5 – Boarding and Reassessment
sections.narrative: When patients board in the ED awaiting psychiatric placement or transfer, risk status and precautions may change over time. The EHR supports time-based reassessment tasks (screening/assessment checkpoints), precaution updates, and continuity during handoffs across ED shifts.

steps.event: Generate reassessment tasks/checkpoints while patient remains in ED (risk, precautions, environment, and observer status)
steps.inputs: Time since last assessment; boarding status; observation level; last room clearance time; protocol rules by risk tier
steps.outputs: Scheduled reassessment Tasks (due time + responsible role); reminders/escalations; completion tracking
steps.actions: EHR schedules reassessment checkpoints (e.g., every X hours, prior to shift change, or before disposition) and escalates if overdue; includes prompts for room re-sweep and observer/precaution review where required
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — Reassessment Cadence PlanDefinition + Reassessment Task profile

steps.event: Reassess suicide risk and update orders/precautions as clinically indicated
steps.inputs: Prior screening/assessment results; current symptoms; new events (agitation, elopement risk); protocol guidance
steps.outputs: Updated risk level/status (discrete); updated precaution orders/parameters; updated safety plan if appropriate
steps.actions: Clinician completes reassessment and updates risk status and precaution orders; EHR makes it easy to modify/discontinue/tailor orders while retaining prior values for audit/longitudinal tracking
steps.profileBinding: Reuses Current Suicide Risk Level Observation (11.4-1B) + Suicide Precaution ServiceRequest (11.3-1B)

steps.event: Re-check environmental safety (room clearance) and confirm observer assignment at shift change / room move
steps.inputs: Current room assignment; last room clearance checklist; observation order/level; staffing assignments
steps.outputs: Updated checklist record (if repeated); updated observer assignment/handoff log; exceptions documented
steps.actions: When the patient remains in the ED or changes rooms, staff repeat the environmental safety sweep per policy and confirm continuous observation coverage (if ordered), documenting completion and any exceptions
steps.walkthroughGapReason: The demo has a single room-clearance event and no shift-change repeat.
steps.fhirText: New instance of Room Clearance Checklist (11.3-1C) + updated `CareTeam` for observer handoff

sections.summary: **Boarding and reassessment** — time-based reassessment during ED boarding.

sections.heading: Scenario 11.6 – Safety Planning and Discharge Planning
sections.narrative: Before ED discharge of a patient with suicide risk, best practice is to create or update a collaborative safety plan, provide lethal means counseling (a distinct intervention), and arrange rapid follow-up. The EHR supports structured, versioned safety plans; structured lethal means safety actions; and discharge-step completion with automatic inclusion/printing of required patient materials.

steps.event: Develop structured safety plan with patient prior to discharge
steps.inputs: Current suicide risk level/status; patient-identified warning signs, coping strategies, supports; crisis resources preferences
steps.outputs: Structured safety plan (versioned) including warning signs, internal coping, supports, professional/crisis resources (incl. 988), and follow-up contacts
steps.actions: Clinician collaborates with patient to complete a structured safety plan template and confirms preferred access method (print and/or portal)

steps.event: Store, version, and make safety plan retrievable across settings
steps.inputs: Structured safety plan data
steps.outputs: Versioned safety plan stored in dedicated chart location; audit trail; linkage to risk status; patient-facing copy-ready artifact
steps.actions: EHR persists and versions the safety plan; supports rapid retrieval for ED and downstream teams; retains prior versions with timestamps
steps.fhirText: `CarePlan` with version history + `Provenance` for each version
steps.profileBinding: Reuses Stanley-Brown CarePlan profile; **gap** — versioning extension
profileGaps: CarePlan versioning extension for Stanley-Brown safety plan

steps.event: Provide lethal means counseling and document agreed actions (stand-alone intervention)
steps.inputs: Means access details (firearms, medications, other); patient/caregiver participants; agreed storage/removal plan
steps.outputs: Discrete lethal-means safety action plan (what/who/where/when) linked to encounter and/or safety plan; education/handout delivery record
steps.actions: Clinician provides lethal means counseling and documents agreed, time-bound means-safety actions; provides education materials and involves supports when appropriate
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — Lethal Means Counseling Procedure + Means-Safety Action profile ([TL-008](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/24), status:planned, promote)

steps.event: Ensure ED discharge requirements are complete for patients with suicide risk
steps.inputs: Risk level/status; completion status of assessment, safety plan, lethal means counseling, and follow-up arrangements
steps.outputs: Discharge readiness checklist status; blocking alerts (if requirements incomplete); compiled AVS package
steps.actions: EHR enforces (or strongly prompts) completion of required elements before discharge and compiles required documents into the AVS/after-visit packet
profileGaps: Discharge Readiness Checklist with blocking behavior

steps.event: Auto-generate and auto-deliver/print safety plan and suicide-specific discharge instructions
steps.inputs: Final safety plan version; local crisis resource directory; patient language/reading level needs; follow-up appointments; patient preferred delivery (print/portal)
steps.outputs: Printed and/or portal-delivered safety plan copy; discharge instructions with psychoeducation and crisis resources; delivery/receipt documentation
steps.actions: At discharge, the EHR automatically includes the safety plan and suicide-specific discharge instructions (including crisis resources and local supports) in the AVS; prints and/or releases to portal per patient preference, and records that materials were delivered

sections.summary: **Safety planning and discharge planning** — collaborative safety plan, lethal means counseling, discharge readiness gating.

sections.heading: Scenario 11.7 – Care Transitions and Follow-Up
sections.narrative: The EHR supports closed-loop care transitions from the ED by transmitting key suicide-related information (as permitted) to next providers, arranging rapid follow-up, and initiating post-discharge contacts (caring contacts and phone follow-up) with monitoring and escalation.

steps.event: Place urgent outpatient follow-up / referral and document disposition plan
steps.inputs: Risk level/status; patient preferences; referral destination; consent/privacy directives
steps.outputs: Referral/AppointmentRequest with urgency; discharge disposition plan; tasks for outreach and follow-up
steps.actions: Clinician places an urgent follow-up request/referral and documents disposition plan, including timeframe and responsible role for scheduling/outreach
steps.fhirText: `ServiceRequest` (urgent outpatient referral) + `Appointment` request + `Communication` to receiving provider
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — Urgent BH Follow-Up Referral profile ([TL-009 Transition](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/25), status:planned, promote)

steps.event: Generate and transmit ED transition-of-care packet
steps.inputs: Screening/assessment outputs; safety plan; lethal-means action plan; demographics; consent/privacy directives
steps.outputs: Transition-of-care packet (electronic); notifications to receiving providers; delivery acknowledgements (when available)
steps.actions: EHR packages and transmits relevant structured information; notifies receiving providers and stores delivery status/acknowledgements when supported
ehrsFm: DC.2.7.1 Care Plan, Guideline, Protocol Generation

steps.event: Initiate post-discharge follow-up protocol (caring contacts and phone calls)
steps.inputs: ED discharge event; risk tier; configured follow-up rules and cadence; patient contact info
steps.outputs: Follow-up Task set (e.g., 24–48h call, 7-day visit); caring contacts schedule; registry/dashboard enrollment
steps.actions: EHR generates protocol-driven follow-up tasks, schedules caring contacts, enrolls patient in a registry/dashboard, and tracks completion and outcomes
steps.fhirText: `Task` series (24–48h call, 7-day visit) + `CommunicationRequest` + `Communication` (per-attempt outreach) + `PlanDefinition` (follow-up cadence) + registry enrollment
steps.profileBinding: **gap** — Caring Contacts PlanDefinition + Caring Contact Task profile ([TL-010](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/26), status:planned, promote); ED-SAFE telephone follow-up profile ([TL-012](https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/issues/28), status:planned, promote) — ED-SAFE specifies the phone-call protocol that Caring Contacts envelopes; both are needed for an ED-anchored follow-up program
profileGaps: Caring Contacts PlanDefinition + Caring Contact Task

steps.event: Conduct follow-up outreach and document outcomes
steps.inputs: Assigned follow-up tasks; patient contact information; safety plan; current risk status
steps.outputs: Outreach documentation; updated risk status (as needed); updated safety plan; next scheduled follow-up
steps.actions: Care team completes outreach per protocol, documents outcomes, updates risk status/safety plan as needed, and schedules next steps

steps.event: Detect missed follow-up and escalate care coordination
steps.inputs: Task status; no-response indicators; missed appointment status; escalation rules
steps.outputs: Escalation alerts; reassigned tasks; documentation of attempted contacts; updated registry status
steps.actions: EHR detects overdue tasks or missed appointments for elevated-risk patients and escalates per protocol (e.g., supervisor alert, additional outreach, welfare check guidance)
steps.fhirText: `Task` status transitions to overdue + `Communication` (supervisor alert) + `Flag` (escalated follow-up status)

sections.summary: **Care transitions and follow-up** — transition-of-care packet, post-discharge caring contacts with overdue escalation.
sections.note: **Gating tools:** Transition (#25), Caring Contacts (#26) — promote priority.

extraWalkthroughSteps.11.7-1A-confirm: Demo-only closed-loop step: a scheduled confirmation that the receiving outpatient BH program got the transition packet. Not in the HL7 scenario, which ends at 11.7-2C.

textPolicy: Source text is normalized ASCII punctuation: U+2011 NON-BREAKING HYPHEN -> "-", curly quotes -> straight. The workbook the working group circulated used U+2011 inside "C-SSRS", "SAFE-T" and "non-acute", which is invisible on screen and defeats exact-match search and joins against every other SPiER document. En dashes and bullets are left alone.

preamble: **First-pass skeleton.** This document captures the structure plus an initial draft mapping of each event step to FHIR resources, profile bindings, and HL7 EHR System Functional Model references. Cells marked *TBD* are open work; cells marked *gap* indicate no SPiER profile exists yet for that artifact.

**Generated** from [`ed-scenario-11.json`](ed-scenario-11.json) by `scripts/build-use-case-workbook.mjs`, alongside the working group's workbook in [`dist/`](dist/). Edit the JSON, not this file. See [`README.md`](README.md).

The clinical scenario itself stays generic — no real patient, no named site, no named vendor. The pseudonymous patient ("Maria, 28, chronic pain and recent job loss") is a scenario archetype, not a real person.
